title: Better by You, better than Me? ChatGPT-3 as writing assistance in students’ essays.
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether using ChatGPT-3 as a writing assistance tool improves students’ essay performance. The authors specifically ask whether ChatGPT support leads to better essay grades, shorter writing time, or differences in text authenticity and similarity compared with traditional essay writing.

The intervention was a one-session essay-writing task in which an experimental group was allowed to use ChatGPT assistance and a control group wrote without it. Students wrote an 800–1000 word essay in Croatian on biometric identification in forensic sciences, and two teachers graded the essays using a rubric covering mechanics, style, content, and format. The study also recorded writing time, plagiarism/unauthenticity scores, pairwise text similarity, and AI-classifier judgments.

The participants were 18 second-year master’s students from the University Department of Forensic Sciences at the University of Split in Croatia. Of 50 students enrolled in the course, 18 volunteered and participated. The authors divided students into control and experimental groups based on study module and weighted GPA to create similar group composition; this indicates matched assignment rather than randomization. The setting appears to be an in-person supervised classroom/lab-style course task at a single university.

The main finding is that ChatGPT assistance did not improve essay quality. Average scores were slightly higher in the control group (2.39 ± 0.71) than in the ChatGPT group (2.00 ± 0.73), with no statistically significant effect of group in the regression model (P = 0.184). Writing time was similar between groups, and the ChatGPT group showed slightly higher unauthenticity percentages. This paper is not the alleged 25+25 secondary-school 12-week randomized motivation trial and provides no motivation outcome. It should not be treated as an RCT, and it is not an appropriate candidate for any extreme effect size claim such as d≈19. For a quantitative synthesis specifically on ChatGPT-based writing feedback in high school, it should be excluded because the population is graduate students rather than high-school students.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a small non-randomized comparative study with only 18 self-selected university students; assignment was done by researchers to balance module and GPA, but the paper does not describe random allocation. It reports quantitative outcomes, but the design has major credibility limitations and is not directly relevant to high-school ChatGPT writing feedback trials.
impact_tier_rationale: The study shows no positive impact of ChatGPT assistance on essay quality or writing efficiency; if anything, the point estimate for writing quality favors the control group. Effects are null/negative and highly uncertain because of the tiny sample.

interventions.use_case: Students used ChatGPT-3 as an essay-writing assistant while composing an 800-1000 word Croatian essay on biometric identification in forensic sciences; the study compares assisted versus unassisted student writing quality, writing time, and text authenticity.

finding.finding_summary: This is a very small comparison study of university master's students, not high-school students. Essay quality did not improve with ChatGPT assistance: the control group mean overall essay score was 2.39 ± 0.71 versus 2.00 ± 0.73 in the ChatGPT group (n=9 per group), and the group effect was not statistically significant in linear regression (P=0.184). A back-of-the-envelope standardized mean difference from the reported means/SDs is approximately d=-0.54 in favor of control, indicating no benefit and possibly worse performance with ChatGPT, but with very high imprecision due to n=18.
finding.measure: Overall essay score averaged across mechanics, style, content, and format, graded A-D and converted to 4-1 numeric scale
finding.effect_size: reported: not_reported; approximate from summary statistics: d≈-0.54 (ChatGPT vs control)

finding.finding_summary: ChatGPT assistance did not reduce writing time. Mean writing duration was 172.22 ± 31.59 minutes in the ChatGPT group versus 179.11 ± 31.93 minutes in the control group (n=9 per group), and writing duration was not a significant predictor of essay score in the regression model (P=0.669). The raw time difference is small, about 6.9 minutes, and corresponds to an approximate effect of d≈-0.22 on time, which is trivial to small.
finding.effect_size: reported: not_reported; approximate from summary statistics: d≈-0.22 for writing time difference
finding.std_deviation: control SD=31.93 minutes; ChatGPT SD=31.59 minutes
